title: Integer arithmetic: compare candidate pairs
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what single skill is this repair problem checking?

source_reference.notes: Called by Q-001 Q001_PAIR_SUM_PRODUCT. Atomicity=num.integer_arithmetic; Scenario=Called by Q-001 Q001_PAIR_SUM_PRODUCT; Surface variation=yes; No new vocab=yes; Steps=1-2. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: Which pair has product 18 and sum 9: 2 and 9, or 3 and 6?
student_prompt: Answer this short repair question. Keep your working brief.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: If 2 and 9 looks correct too quickly, the issue is checking only one condition. Quadratic factorising needs both the product and middle-term sum to be true.

hint_ladder.title: Check each pair
hint_ladder.prompt: The question gives two candidate pairs. Test the product and the sum for each pair instead of choosing by sight.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply first
hint_ladder.prompt: For each candidate pair, calculate the product and the sum in a small table. Choose only the pair that passes both checks.

hint_ladder.title: Looks plausible
hint_ladder.prompt: A pair can match one condition without matching the whole question. Check product 18 and sum 9 before choosing.

hint_ladder.title: Candidate routine
hint_ladder.prompt: When candidates are provided, make a two-column product/sum check for each option. Use the numbers here; do not copy.

common_errors: uses the previous larger problem instead of this repair skill
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: This repair focuses on comparing candidate pairs systematically, not just recognising one pair that seems related to the numbers in the question.
